answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks through quadratic influence pricing, where each extra identity a single actor controls costs quadratically more. Ten votes from ten puppet accounts cost a hundred times the base price rather than ten, so an attacker must forge real capital to dominate. A sybil ring cannot simply bend like a willow and sprout cheap identities; it must pay a saffron tier stake for every fake agent. Because cost scales with the square while influence scales with its square root, multiplying accounts drains the attacker's treasury and buys no extra sway.
